name: Blue Pill (STM32F103C8T6)
description: The $2-3 STM32F103 Cortex-M3 board: 72 MHz, 64/128 KB flash, 2x20 breadboard pins, micro-USB; the cheapest ARM board, but older and full of clone-chip and USB-resistor gotchas.
notes: Genuine ST chips are rare: many boards carry CKS32F103, APM32F103 or GD32F103 clones (some with 128 KB flash enabled); behaviour and USB can differ.

The USB D+ pull-up resistor (R10) is often 10 k instead of 1.5 k, which breaks USB enumeration on some hosts; swap it. No ROM USB DFU on F103: flash with ST-Link (SWD header) or the UART bootloader (BOOT0 jumper).
5 V pins connect straight to USB VBUS with no protection. PC13 LED is active-low. No mechanical drawing verified, so no header data.
For a modern replacement use a WeAct Black Pill (F411/G431) at similar cost.
